claims.statement: Physiotherapy may be considered before surgical management of rectus diastasis; no particular exercise programme or improvement in symptoms can be guaranteed from the guideline evidence.
claims.limitation: Targeted KQ6 verification, weak recommendation. Applying this alongside observation of a separate asymptomatic primary hernia is a combined clinical inference requiring review, not a trial-proven sequence for all concomitant defects.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: For isolated rectus diastasis selected for surgery, plication with or without mesh augmentation is described, without an established universal preference among techniques.
claims.limitation: Targeted KQ7 verification. This limitation is used to park an underdetermined technique comparison, not to score a preferred operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A superficial wound swab does not establish the microbiology of a separate deep periprosthetic pocket. Depth must be assessed from the clinical, imaging and operative context, with the sampled compartment identified.
claims.limitation: The cohort defined depth from clinical/surgical/imaging findings and excluded superficial swabs from etiologic cultures. This is a compartment-provenance inference, not a validated diagnostic-accuracy rule or proof that a swab is always contamination.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Cephalexin is a labeled option for skin or skin-structure infection caused by susceptible Staphylococcus aureus; antibacterial treatment requires a proven or strongly suspected clinical bacterial infection.
claims.limitation: Official-label fact supports the distractor's counterfactual superficial infection, not treatment of a deep implant focus. No dose, duration, allergy selection or empiric regimen is scored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A persistent symptomatic seroma may undergo sterile aspiration; symptomatic recurrence after aspiration can lead to operative drainage and treatment of the lining.
claims.limitation: Single older society guideline, low-quality evidence. Distinguish a never-aspirated symptomatic pocket from symptomatic recurrence after aspiration; no mandatory time or number-of-aspirations threshold is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A reproducible focal midline protrusion can establish a primary ventral hernia clinically; a nonreproducible examination leaves uncertainty requiring targeted assessment.
claims.limitation: No routine MRI rule or exact imaging accuracy claim is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Watchful waiting can be considered for an asymptomatic reducible umbilical or epigastric hernia.
claims.limitation: Weak recommendation and a single directly verified guideline. Not extended here to persistent work-limiting symptoms.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Cross-sectional imaging is appropriate when planning incisional hernia repair or when examination does not resolve the diagnosis.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. CT is sensitive; ultrasound or MRI can be appropriate alternatives. No universal IV-contrast requirement is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Activity-limiting symptoms from a reducible hernia support elective surgical evaluation, with repair weighed against operative risks and the patient's goals.
claims.limitation: Decision principles span primary/incisional hernias; not a mandate for one approach or a numerical quality-of-life threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A reducible incisional hernia without troublesome symptoms can be managed with observation after discussing repair risks and acute warning symptoms.
claims.limitation: One guideline; observation is revisited if symptoms change. No individual risk percentage or guaranteed safety is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: New irreducibility with obstructive symptoms or concerning local/systemic findings requires urgent hospital surgical assessment.
claims.limitation: Not a validated score or proof that all incarcerated contents are ischemic. Elective pulmonary optimization does not replace this assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Reduced enhancement of bowel trapped in a hernia, interpreted with acute pain and local peritoneal findings, raises concern for strangulation and warrants emergency operative assessment.
claims.limitation: One targeted guideline; no single imaging sign is perfectly sensitive and a normal lactate is not used to exclude ischemia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A defect beside the rectus through the semilunar-region aponeurosis may contain fat or bowel between abdominal-wall layers.
claims.limitation: Targeted society guidance; no protected anatomical figure reproduced, and no demographic selection weight authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Examination with targeted ultrasonography or CT can evaluate suspected Spigelian hernia; a resting examination can miss an intermittent interparietal protrusion.
claims.limitation: Weak guideline. Dynamic acquisition answers the constructed intermittent presentation; ultrasound is not declared universally superior to CT.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A confirmed symptomatic Spigelian hernia merits repair evaluation; mesh repair is suggested, while evidence does not establish one universal open or laparoscopic approach.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline; technique ranking is intentionally not scored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Rectus diastasis widens the linea alba rather than creating the focal fascial opening of a hernia; a separate focal defect can coexist.
claims.limitation: No exact inter-rectus threshold is needed in these items. The two society documents have overlapping authorship and are not treated as independent trials.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Physiotherapy can be considered before operative treatment of symptomatic rectus diastasis without a concomitant hernia.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline; no proven exercise protocol, response guarantee or required duration.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: When a symptomatic midline hernia coexists with rectus diastasis and repair is chosen, mesh-based repair is suggested over treating the hernia as an isolated suture defect.
claims.limitation: Weak recommendations; very small defects and individual goals need clinical review. No mandatory simultaneous diastasis operation is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Retrorectus mesh lies between rectus muscle and posterior sheath; preperitoneal mesh lies deeper, between the posterior sheath and peritoneum.
claims.limitation: One directly checked society guideline; these descriptions concern the region with a posterior sheath. No assertion that all subarcuate anatomy is identical.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: For elective midline incisional repair within its scope, EHS guidance favors retromuscular mesh placement and caution with implants exposed to viscera.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty for plane preference. This is not the emergency onlay recommendation or a mandate when the plane is unavailable.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A feasible midline incisional repair aims to close the fascial defect with mesh reinforcement rather than bridge an open defect.
claims.limitation: Anticipated closable elective scope. Posterior-layer closure alone does not restore the anterior fascial defect; forceful closure is not endorsed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A wide recurrent incisional defect may require myofascial release expertise; CT helps plan complexity but does not prove that a particular release is required.
claims.limitation: One guideline. The guideline's width-over-8-cm planning signal is not a universal operative cutoff; the fictional 12-cm case is well beyond the signal.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Pulmonary fitness, glycemic control, smoking and weight are modifiable considerations before elective incisional repair.
claims.limitation: No exact medication, target BMI, HbA1c value, cessation interval or mandatory delay is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: After an unsuccessful dedicated weight-loss effort, progressive symptoms and enlargement can favor proceeding to a repair discussion rather than delaying indefinitely for more weight loss.
claims.limitation: One good-practice statement, not an automatic surgery rule or exemption from risk counseling.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: For a reducible primary midline hernia with tolerable symptoms, repair can be deferred until after the last planned pregnancy because subsequent pregnancy increases recurrence risk.
claims.limitation: Weak guideline; worsening symptoms, incarceration or inability to defer alter the decision. Exact mesh-versus-suture policy if deferral is impossible is withheld.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Postoperative skin erythema does not by itself establish infection of a prosthesis; a draining deep tract or periprosthetic infected collection warrants evaluation of the implant plane.
claims.limitation: Guideline plus observational depth assessment; no CT finding independently proves infection or excludes a bowel fistula.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Selected stable patients with infected hernia mesh may undergo a specialist-directed salvage attempt using antibiotics, drainage and/or wound debridement.
claims.limitation: Older guideline plus observational selection evidence; no universal success rate or material-specific probability is claimed. Sepsis, chronicity and persistent infection change the decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Persistent mesh infection after a completed conservative source-control attempt supports mesh excision assessment; sepsis requires urgent surgical source control.
claims.limitation: Guideline plus independent observational recurrence evidence. Excision extent and subsequent reconstruction must be decided by the treating surgical team; not an outpatient office procedure.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: An asymptomatic postoperative seroma after ventral mesh repair can be observed; persistent symptomatic collections may warrant sterile drainage assessment.
claims.limitation: Low-quality evidence, single older guideline; infection, recurrent fascial defect and symptom trajectory must be assessed separately. No calendar cutoff invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: In a stable emergency ventral-hernia patient after source control, inability to directly close fascia supports deferring definitive abdominal-wall reconstruction rather than undertaking immediate advanced release.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty conditional recommendation. Differs from abandoning abdominal-cavity closure or mandating an open abdomen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: When an emergency patient is stable and source control is adequate, abdominal-cavity closure using available skin or sac can be appropriate even though fascial reconstruction is deferred.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty conditional guidance; not applicable when ongoing resuscitation, uncertain bowel viability or compartment concerns require an open abdomen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Continuing resuscitation, bowel requiring a second look, or concern for pressure-related organ dysfunction can justify temporary abdominal closure rather than definitive fascial reconstruction.
claims.limitation: No pressure cutoff, exact second-look interval or universal open-abdomen rule taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: After adequate source control in a stable selected single-stage ventral repair, a controlled bowel entry does not automatically require a biologic implant; current emergency guidance favors permanent macroporous synthetic mesh when mesh repair is selected.
claims.limitation: Not a blanket instruction to complete every enterotomy case in one stage or place uncoated mesh against bowel. Frozen approved material rules remain exact.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Elective midline laparotomy closure is supported by continuous small aponeurotic bites with slowly absorbable suture, adequate suture length and low tension.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline. The stated suture-to-wound length ratio of at least 4:1 directly supports the constructed arithmetic comparison; not an emergency closure protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: The elective midline small-bites technique uses a suture-to-wound length ratio of at least 4:1.
claims.limitation: Direct numerical support in the guideline's technique description. Not an isolated validated success guarantee or an emergency threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Prophylactic mesh augmentation can be considered after elective midline laparotomy closure; permanent synthetic onlay or retromuscular placement is suggested when augmentation is selected.
claims.limitation: Weak guidance; augmentation does not replace a technically appropriate primary closure. This is not a routine trocar-site mesh recommendation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Fascial closure is suggested for adult trocar defects of 10 mm or greater, especially at the umbilicus; assessment concerns the final fascial opening.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty, weak guideline. Final-opening application is a clinical inference; no optimal suture material or routine prophylactic mesh recommendation established for ports.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

holds.reason: Older WSES contaminated/dirty biologic-mesh guidance and newer EHS source-controlled emergency guidance differ in scope and recommendation. Do not extend the selected controlled-enterotomy rule to continuing leakage, sepsis or any unclosable defect, or substitute a universal biologic rule.

holds.reason: Complexity referral is supported; an exact botulinum-toxin, progressive-pneumoperitoneum or mandatory TAR regimen is not verified in this packet. No dose, volume or timing is invented.

Round 2: 3 editorial PASS preserved; 10 revised candidates still pending independent re-review; 10 concrete attempts parked. No automatic or author-conferred PASS.
Four new concept meanings reflect changed objectives; all old IDs and mapping history retained. No original coverage retired.

New-source claims do not turn the retrospective cohort into a patient-level treatment trial. A positive surface swab is not treated as proof that infection is absent or present in a different unsampled compartment.

claims.statement: A reproducible focal midline protrusion can establish a primary ventral hernia clinically; a nonreproducible examination leaves uncertainty requiring targeted assessment.
claims.limitation: No routine MRI rule or exact imaging accuracy claim is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Watchful waiting can be considered for an asymptomatic reducible umbilical or epigastric hernia.
claims.limitation: Weak recommendation and a single directly verified guideline. Not extended here to persistent work-limiting symptoms.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Cross-sectional imaging is appropriate when planning incisional hernia repair or when examination does not resolve the diagnosis.
claims.limitation: One directly checked guideline. CT is sensitive; ultrasound or MRI can be appropriate alternatives. No universal IV-contrast requirement is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Activity-limiting symptoms from a reducible hernia support elective surgical evaluation, with repair weighed against operative risks and the patient's goals.
claims.limitation: Decision principles span primary/incisional hernias; not a mandate for one approach or a numerical quality-of-life threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A reducible incisional hernia without troublesome symptoms can be managed with observation after discussing repair risks and acute warning symptoms.
claims.limitation: One guideline; observation is revisited if symptoms change. No individual risk percentage or guaranteed safety is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: New irreducibility with obstructive symptoms or concerning local/systemic findings requires urgent hospital surgical assessment.
claims.limitation: Not a validated score or proof that all incarcerated contents are ischemic. Elective pulmonary optimization does not replace this assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Reduced enhancement of bowel trapped in a hernia, interpreted with acute pain and local peritoneal findings, raises concern for strangulation and warrants emergency operative assessment.
claims.limitation: One targeted guideline; no single imaging sign is perfectly sensitive and a normal lactate is not used to exclude ischemia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A defect beside the rectus through the semilunar-region aponeurosis may contain fat or bowel between abdominal-wall layers.
claims.limitation: Targeted society guidance; no protected anatomical figure reproduced, and no demographic selection weight authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Examination with targeted ultrasonography or CT can evaluate suspected Spigelian hernia; a resting examination can miss an intermittent interparietal protrusion.
claims.limitation: Weak guideline. Dynamic acquisition answers the constructed intermittent presentation; ultrasound is not declared universally superior to CT.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A confirmed symptomatic Spigelian hernia merits repair evaluation; mesh repair is suggested, while evidence does not establish one universal open or laparoscopic approach.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline; technique ranking is intentionally not scored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Rectus diastasis widens the linea alba rather than creating the focal fascial opening of a hernia; a separate focal defect can coexist.
claims.limitation: No exact inter-rectus threshold is needed in these items. The two society documents have overlapping authorship and are not treated as independent trials.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Physiotherapy can be considered before operative treatment of symptomatic rectus diastasis without a concomitant hernia.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline; no proven exercise protocol, response guarantee or required duration.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: When a symptomatic midline hernia coexists with rectus diastasis and repair is chosen, mesh-based repair is suggested over treating the hernia as an isolated suture defect.
claims.limitation: Weak recommendations; very small defects and individual goals need clinical review. No mandatory simultaneous diastasis operation is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Retrorectus mesh lies between rectus muscle and posterior sheath; preperitoneal mesh lies deeper, between the posterior sheath and peritoneum.
claims.limitation: One directly checked society guideline; these descriptions concern the region with a posterior sheath. No assertion that all subarcuate anatomy is identical.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: For elective midline incisional repair within its scope, EHS guidance favors retromuscular mesh placement and caution with implants exposed to viscera.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty for plane preference. This is not the emergency onlay recommendation or a mandate when the plane is unavailable.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A feasible midline incisional repair aims to close the fascial defect with mesh reinforcement rather than bridge an open defect.
claims.limitation: Anticipated closable elective scope. Posterior-layer closure alone does not restore the anterior fascial defect; forceful closure is not endorsed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: A wide recurrent incisional defect may require myofascial release expertise; CT helps plan complexity but does not prove that a particular release is required.
claims.limitation: One guideline. The guideline's width-over-8-cm planning signal is not a universal operative cutoff; the fictional 12-cm case is well beyond the signal.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Pulmonary fitness, glycemic control, smoking and weight are modifiable considerations before elective incisional repair.
claims.limitation: No exact medication, target BMI, HbA1c value, cessation interval or mandatory delay is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: After an unsuccessful dedicated weight-loss effort, progressive symptoms and enlargement can favor proceeding to a repair discussion rather than delaying indefinitely for more weight loss.
claims.limitation: One good-practice statement, not an automatic surgery rule or exemption from risk counseling.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: For a reducible primary midline hernia with tolerable symptoms, repair can be deferred until after the last planned pregnancy because subsequent pregnancy increases recurrence risk.
claims.limitation: Weak guideline; worsening symptoms, incarceration or inability to defer alter the decision. Exact mesh-versus-suture policy if deferral is impossible is withheld.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Postoperative skin erythema does not by itself establish infection of a prosthesis; a draining deep tract or periprosthetic infected collection warrants evaluation of the implant plane.
claims.limitation: Guideline plus observational depth assessment; no CT finding independently proves infection or excludes a bowel fistula.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Selected stable patients with infected hernia mesh may undergo a specialist-directed salvage attempt using antibiotics, drainage and/or wound debridement.
claims.limitation: Older guideline plus observational selection evidence; no universal success rate or material-specific probability is claimed. Sepsis, chronicity and persistent infection change the decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Persistent mesh infection after a completed conservative source-control attempt supports mesh excision assessment; sepsis requires urgent surgical source control.
claims.limitation: Guideline plus independent observational recurrence evidence. Excision extent and subsequent reconstruction must be decided by the treating surgical team; not an outpatient office procedure.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: An asymptomatic postoperative seroma after ventral mesh repair can be observed; persistent symptomatic collections may warrant sterile drainage assessment.
claims.limitation: Low-quality evidence, single older guideline; infection, recurrent fascial defect and symptom trajectory must be assessed separately. No calendar cutoff invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: In a stable emergency ventral-hernia patient after source control, inability to directly close fascia supports deferring definitive abdominal-wall reconstruction rather than undertaking immediate advanced release.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty conditional recommendation. Differs from abandoning abdominal-cavity closure or mandating an open abdomen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: When an emergency patient is stable and source control is adequate, abdominal-cavity closure using available skin or sac can be appropriate even though fascial reconstruction is deferred.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty conditional guidance; not applicable when ongoing resuscitation, uncertain bowel viability or compartment concerns require an open abdomen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Continuing resuscitation, bowel requiring a second look, or concern for pressure-related organ dysfunction can justify temporary abdominal closure rather than definitive fascial reconstruction.
claims.limitation: No pressure cutoff, exact second-look interval or universal open-abdomen rule taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: After adequate source control in a stable selected single-stage ventral repair, a controlled bowel entry does not automatically require a biologic implant; current emergency guidance favors permanent macroporous synthetic mesh when mesh repair is selected.
claims.limitation: Not a blanket instruction to complete every enterotomy case in one stage or place uncoated mesh against bowel. Frozen approved material rules remain exact.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Elective midline laparotomy closure is supported by continuous small aponeurotic bites with slowly absorbable suture, adequate suture length and low tension.
claims.limitation: Single weak guideline. The stated suture-to-wound length ratio of at least 4:1 directly supports the constructed arithmetic comparison; not an emergency closure protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: The elective midline small-bites technique uses a suture-to-wound length ratio of at least 4:1.
claims.limitation: Direct numerical support in the guideline's technique description. Not an isolated validated success guarantee or an emergency threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Prophylactic mesh augmentation can be considered after elective midline laparotomy closure; permanent synthetic onlay or retromuscular placement is suggested when augmentation is selected.
claims.limitation: Weak guidance; augmentation does not replace a technically appropriate primary closure. This is not a routine trocar-site mesh recommendation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

claims.statement: Fascial closure is suggested for adult trocar defects of 10 mm or greater, especially at the umbilicus; assessment concerns the final fascial opening.
claims.limitation: Very-low certainty, weak guideline. Final-opening application is a clinical inference; no optimal suture material or routine prophylactic mesh recommendation established for ports.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact constructed clinic encounters and outside-hospital chart reviews; see individual scope boundaries.

holds.reason: The 2026 emergency guideline suggests onlay with very-low-certainty evidence, while the 2023 elective guideline favors retromuscular placement. Different populations do not support a universal preferred plane. No emergency onlay-vs-retromuscular scored key is authored.
holds.nextAction: Melissa and independent reviewer should define a clinically specific emergency plane comparison before any additional scored item.

holds.reason: Older WSES contaminated/dirty biologic-mesh guidance and newer EHS source-controlled emergency guidance differ in scope and recommendation. Do not extend the selected controlled-enterotomy rule to continuing leakage, sepsis or any unclosable defect, or substitute a universal biologic rule.
holds.nextAction: Keep disputed all-dirty-field material teaching unkeyed; clinician must specify source control, physiology, defect and closure context.

holds.reason: Complexity referral is supported; an exact botulinum-toxin, progressive-pneumoperitoneum or mandatory TAR regimen is not verified in this packet. No dose, volume or timing is invented.
holds.nextAction: Targeted primary guidance and named reconstructive clinician review before drafting adjunct-regimen keys.

holds.reason: Deferral is supported when symptoms allow. A patient who cannot defer requires a separate weak-evidence mesh-versus-suture tradeoff; this packet does not score one universal material answer.
holds.nextAction: Melissa should define exact symptom, preference and future-pregnancy constraints if this further item is wanted.

holds.reason: Inherited quality park is unresolved. Merely stating that closure is readily feasible creates a basic answer; removing feasibility makes a release/tension choice unfair. No new exact closure-layer question is presented as a successful repair of that parked item.
holds.nextAction: Manager preserves the parked original. The separate complex-planning draft assesses referral scope and does not clear this park.
